verses.text: For you, Lord, I don take refuge. Make I no ever shame.
Deliver me for your righteousness and rescue me. Bend your ear to me and save me.
Be my rock of refuge, wey I fit always go. You don give command to save me, because you be my rock and my fortress.
My God, rescue me from di hand of di wicked, from di grasp of unjust and cruel man.
Because you be my hope, Lord God. You be my trust from my youth.
I don lean on you from birth. Na you take me from my mama womb. My praise go always dey for you.
I don be like wonder to many, but you be my strong refuge.
My mouth dey full of your praise and of your honor all di day.
No throw me away for time of old age. No leave me when my strength fail.
Because my enemies dey talk about me. Dem wey dey watch my soul dey plan together,
dey talk say, “God don leave am. Chase am and catch am, because nobody dey to deliver.”
God, no dey far from me. My God, hurry to help me.
Make dem shame and consumed, dem wey be adversaries to my soul. Make dem wey seek my hurt cover with reproach and dishonor.
But I go hope always. I go praise you more and more.
My mouth go tell of your righteousness and your salvation all day, because I no know di number of dem.
I go come with di mighty acts of di Lord God. I go make mention of your righteousness, yours only.
God, you don teach me from my youth. Until now I don declare your wonderful works.
Yes, even when I old and gray, God, no forsake me, until I declare your strength to di next generation, your might to all wey go come.
Your righteousness also, God, reach to di heights. You wey don do great things, God, who be like you?
You, wey don show me many and bitter troubles, go revive me again and go bring me up again from di depths of di earth.
Increase my greatness and comfort me again.
I go also praise you with harp, for your truth, my God. I go sing praises to you with lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips go shout for joy when I sing praises to you, and my soul wey you don redeem.
My tongue go also talk about your righteousness all day long, because dem don shame, because dem don disgrace, dem wey seek my hurt.
Give di king your justice, God, and your righteousness to di king son.
E go judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
Di mountains go bring peace to di people, and di hills go bring righteousness.
E go judge di poor of di people. E go save di pikin dem of di needy and go break di oppressor to pieces.
Dem go fear you as long as di sun and moon dey, throughout all generations.
E go come down like rain on di mown grass, like showers wey water di earth.
For im days di righteous go flourish, and plenty peace go dey until di moon no dey again.
E go rule from sea to sea, and from di River to di ends of di earth.
Dem wey dey live for di desert go bow before am, and im enemies go lick di dust.
Di kings of Tarshish and of di islands go bring tribute. Di kings of Sheba and Seba go offer gifts.
Yes, all kings go bow down before am. All nations go serve am.
Because e go deliver di needy when e cry, di poor also, and am wey no get helper.
E go have pity on di poor and needy. E go save di souls of di needy.
E go redeem dem soul from oppression and violence. Dem blood go dey precious for im sight.
Make e live! Make dem give am gold of Sheba. Make dem pray for am continually. Make dem bless am all day long.
Make plenty grain dey for di land on top of di mountains. Make im fruit shake like Lebanon. Make dem for di cities flourish like grass of di field.
Make im name endure forever. Make im name continue as long as di sun. Make men bless dem self by am. Make all nations call am blessed.
Blessed be di Lord God, di God of Israel, wey only dey do wonderful things.
Blessed be im glorious name forever. Make di whole earth full of im glory. Amen and amen.
Di prayers of David, di son of Jesse, don end.
Surely God dey good to Israel, to dem wey get clean heart.
But as for me, my feet nearly slip. My steps nearly go astray.
Because I dey envy di arrogant when I see di prosperity of di wicked.
Because dem no get pain for dem death. Dem body strong and fat.
Dem no dey for di trouble wey other men dey. Dem no dey plagued like other men.
So pride na di necklace wey dem wear. Violence cover dem like cloth.
Dem eyes dey bulge with fat. Dem hearts dey overflow with imagination.
Dem dey mock and speak with malice. Dem dey speak oppression from on high.
Dem set dem mouth against di heavens, and dem tongue dey waka through di earth.
So im people return to dem, and dem drink plenty water.
Dem talk say, “How God go know? Di Most High get knowledge?”
Look, dis na di wicked, and dem dey at ease forever. Dem dey increase for riches.
Sure sure I don keep my heart clean for nothing and wash my hands for innocence.
Because all day I dey plagued and dey punished every morning.
If I don talk say, “I go speak so,” I don betray di generation of your pikin dem.
When I think how to understand dis, e too hard for me,
until I enter di sanctuary of God and consider dem end.
Surely you set dem for slippery places. You throw dem down to destruction.
How dem become desolate sudden sudden! Terrors don completely sweep dem away.
Like dream when person wake up, Lord, when you wake, you go despise dem image.
For my heart dey grieved, and my spirit dey pierced.
I be foolish and ignorant. I be like animal before you.
Even so, I dey with you always. You don hold my right hand.
You go guide me with your counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
Who I get for heaven but you? And on earth nothing I desire beside you.
My flesh and my heart fail, but God na di strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Because look, dem wey dey far from you go perish. You don destroy all dem wey go astray from you.
But as for me, na good to dey near God. I don make di Lord God my refuge, so dat I go tell all your works.
God, why you don reject us forever? Why your anger dey burn against di sheep of your pasture?
Remember your congregation, wey you don buy long ago, di tribe of your inheritance wey you don redeem, dis Mount Zion, where you don dwell.
Lift up your steps to di perpetual ruins, all di damage wey di enemy don do for di sanctuary.
Your adversaries roar inside your meeting place. Dem don set up dem own banners as signs.
Dem dey like men wey lift up axes for thick forest.
Now all im carved work dem dey break down with hatchet and hammer.
Dem don set your sanctuary on fire. Dem don defile di dwelling place of your name to di ground.
Dem talk for dem heart say, “We go crush dem completely.” Dem don burn up all di meeting places of God for di land.
We no see our signs. No prophet dey again, and nobody among us know how long.
How long, God, di adversary go reproach? Di enemy go blaspheme your name forever?
Why you dey hold back your hand, your right hand? Take am from your chest and consume dem.
Yet God na my King from old, wey dey work salvation for di middle of di earth.
You divide di sea by your strength. You break di heads of di sea monsters for di waters.
You crush di heads of Leviathan. You give am as food to di people wey dey for di wilderness.
You open spring and flood. You dry up ever flowing rivers.
Di day na your own, di night also na your own. You don prepare di light and di sun.
You don set all di borders of di earth. You make summer and winter.
Remember dis, Lord: di enemy don reproach, and foolish people don blaspheme your name.
No deliver di soul of your dove to di wild animal. No forget di life of your poor forever.
Consider di covenant, because di dark places of di earth full of homes of violence.
No let di oppressed return ashamed. Make di poor and needy praise your name.
Arise, God, plead your own cause. Remember how di foolish man dey reproach you all day.
No forget di voice of your adversaries, di uproar of dem wey rise up against you, wey dey go up continually.

chapters.title: For di Chief Musician. To di tune of Do Not Destroy. A Psalm by Asaph. A song.

verses.text: We give thanks to you, God. We give thanks, because your name dey near. Men dey tell of your wonderful works.
“When I choose di appointed time, I go judge with fairness.
Di earth and all dem wey dey live inside am dey melt away. Na me hold im pillars steady. Selah.
I talk to di arrogant say, ‘No dey arrogant,’ and to di wicked, ‘No lift up di horn.
No lift up your horn on high. No speak with stiff neck.’”
Because lifting up no dey come from di east, or from di west, or from di south.
But God na di judge. E dey put down one and lift up another.
Because for di hand of di Lord dey cup, with foaming wine, well mixed. E dey pour out from am, and all di wicked of di earth go drain am and drink am to di dregs.
But I go declare am forever. I go sing praises to di God of Jacob.
“I go cut off all di horns of di wicked, but di horns of di righteous go dey lifted up.”

chapters.title: For di Chief Musician. With stringed instruments. A Psalm by Asaph. A song.

verses.text: God dey known for Judah. Im name great for Israel.
Im tent dey for Salem, and im dwelling place for Zion.
Dere e break di flaming arrows, di shield, di sword and di weapons of war. Selah.
You dey glorious and excellent, more pass di mountains of prey.
Di brave of heart don dey plundered. Dem don sleep dem sleep. None of di mighty men fit find dem hands.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse don fall into deep sleep.
You, na you suppose dey feared. Who fit stand for your sight when your anger dey?
You cause judgment to dey heard from heaven. Di earth fear and dey quiet
when God arise to judgment, to save all di humble of di earth. Selah.
Surely di wrath of man go praise you. You go gird yourself with di remainder of wrath.
Make vows and pay dem to di Lord una God. Make all wey dey around am bring gifts to am wey suppose dey feared.
E dey cut off di spirit of princes. E dey awesome to di kings of di earth.

chapters.title: For di Chief Musician. For Jeduthun. A Psalm by Asaph.

verses.text: I go cry aloud to God, yes, aloud to God, and e go hear me.
For di day of my trouble I seek di Lord. My hand dey stretched out for night and no tire. My soul refuse to dey comforted.
I remember God, and I dey troubled. I complain, and my spirit dey overwhelmed. Selah.
You hold my eyelids open. I dey too troubled to speak.
I consider di days of old, di years of long ago.
I remember my song for di night. I think for my heart, and my spirit dey search.
Di Lord go reject forever? E no go show favor again?
Im faithful love don finish forever? Im promise don fail forevermore?
God don forget to dey gracious? E don shut im tender mercies for anger? Selah.
I talk say, “Dis na my sorrow: di years of di right hand of di Most High.”
I go remember di works of di Lord. Yes, I go remember your wonders of old.
I go also meditate on all your work and think about your deeds.
Your way, God, dey holy. Which god dey great like God?
You be di God wey dey do wonders. You don make your strength known among di peoples.
You don redeem your people with your arm, di sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
Di waters see you, God. Di waters see you and dey afraid. Di depths also tremble.
Di clouds pour out water. Di skies thunder. Your arrows also flash around.
Di voice of your thunder dey for di whirlwind. Di lightnings light up di world. Di earth tremble and shake.
Your way dey for di sea, and your paths for di great waters, and your footsteps no dey known.
You lead your people like flock by di hand of Moses and Aaron.
Hear my law, my people. Bend your ears to di words of my mouth.
I go open my mouth for parable. I go speak hidden things from of old,
wetin we don hear and know, wetin our papa dem don tell us.
We no go hide dem from dem pikin dem, but go tell di generation to come di praises of di Lord, im strength and di wonderful works wey e don do.
Because e establish testimony for Jacob and appoint law for Israel, wey e command our papa dem, so dat dem go make dem known to dem pikin dem,
so dat di next generation go know dem, even di pikin dem wey go dey born, wey go rise up and tell dem to dem pikin dem,
so dat dem go set dem hope for God and no forget di works of God, but keep im commandments,
and no go be like dem papa dem, stubborn and rebellious generation, generation wey no prepare dem heart and wey dem spirit no dey faithful to God.
Di sons of Ephraim, armed with bows, turn back for di day of battle.
Dem no keep di covenant of God and refuse to waka for im law.
Dem forget wetin e don do and im wonders wey e don show dem.
E do marvelous things for di sight of dem papa dem, for di land of Egypt, for di field of Zoan.
E divide di sea and make dem pass through, and e make di waters stand like heap.
For daytime e lead dem with cloud and all di night with light of fire.
E split rocks for di wilderness and give dem drink as from great depths.
E bring streams out of di rock and make waters run down like rivers.
Yet dem continue to sin more against am, to rebel against di Most High for di desert.
Dem test God for dem heart by asking for food wey dem crave.
Yes, dem speak against God. Dem talk say, “God fit prepare table for di wilderness?
Look, e strike di rock so dat waters gush out and streams overflow. E fit give bread too? E fit provide meat for im people?”
So di Lord hear and e vex. Fire burn against Jacob, and anger also rise against Israel,
because dem no believe for God and no trust im salvation.
Yet e command di skies above and open di doors of heaven.
E rain down manna on dem to eat and give dem grain of heaven.
Man eat di bread of angels. E send dem food to di full.
E cause di east wind to blow for heaven. By im power e lead out di south wind.
E rain meat on dem like dust, and winged birds like sand of di seas.
E make dem fall inside dem camp, round dem dwellings.
So dem eat and satisfy well. E give dem wetin dem crave.
Dem never turn from dem craving, even while dem food still dey dem mouths,
di anger of God rise against dem, and e kill di strongest of dem and strike down di young men of Israel.
For all dis dem still sin and no believe im wonderful works.
So e end dem days for vanity and dem years for terror.
When e kill dem, dem seek am. Dem return and look for God earnestly.
Dem remember say God na dem rock, and God Most High na dem redeemer.
But dem flatter am with dem mouth and lie to am with dem tongue.
Dem heart no dey right with am, and dem no dey faithful for im covenant.
But e wey full of mercy forgive iniquity and no destroy dem. Many times e turn im anger away and no stir up all im wrath.
E remember say dem na flesh, wind wey pass and no return.
How many times dem rebel against am for di wilderness and grieve am for di desert!
Dem turn back and test God again, and provoke di Holy One of Israel.
Dem no remember im hand, or di day wey e redeem dem from di adversary,
how e do im signs for Egypt and im wonders for di field of Zoan.
E turn dem rivers to blood and dem streams, so dat dem no fit drink.
E send among dem swarms of flies wey devour dem, and frogs wey destroy dem.
E give dem crops to di caterpillar and dem labor to di locust.
E destroy dem vines with hail and dem sycamore trees with frost.
E give dem livestock to di hail and dem flocks to bolts of lightning.
E send on dem im fierce anger, wrath, indignation and trouble, band of destroying angels.
E make way for im anger. E no spare dem soul from death, but give dem life to di plague.
E strike all di firstborn for Egypt, di first of dem strength for di tents of Ham.
But e lead out im own people like sheep and guide dem for di wilderness like flock.
E lead dem safely, so dem no fear, but di sea overwhelm dem enemies.
E bring dem to di border of im holy land, to di hill country wey im right hand don win.
E drive out di nations before dem, measure dem out as inheritance and make di tribes of Israel dwell for dem tents.
Yet dem test and rebel against God Most High and no keep im testimonies,
but turn back and dey unfaithful like dem papa dem. Dem turn aside like unreliable bow.
Because dem provoke am to anger with dem high places and move am to jealousy with dem idols.
When God hear, e vex and greatly reject Israel,
so e abandon di tabernacle of Shiloh, di tent wey e put among men,
and give im strength to captivity and im glory to di enemy hand.
E give im people to di sword and vex with im inheritance.
Fire consume dem young men, and dem young women no get wedding songs.
Dem priests fall by di sword, and dem widows no fit weep.
Den di Lord wake up like man wey dey sleep, like strong man wey shout because of wine.
E strike im adversaries back. E put dem to everlasting shame.
Moreover e reject di tent of Joseph and no choose di tribe of Ephraim,
but e choose di tribe of Judah, Mount Zion wey e love.
E build im sanctuary like di heights, like di earth wey e don establish forever.
E also choose David im servant and take am from di sheepfolds.
From following di ewes wey get young, e bring am to shepherd Jacob im people and Israel im inheritance.
So e shepherd dem according to di integrity of im heart and guide dem with di skillfulness of im hands.
God, di nations don come into your inheritance. Dem don defile your holy temple. Dem don make Jerusalem heaps of ruins.
Dem don give di dead bodies of your servants as food to di birds of di sky, di flesh of your holy ones to di animals of di earth.
Dem don pour out dem blood like water round Jerusalem, and nobody dey to bury dem.
We don become reproach to our neighbors, scorn and derision to dem wey dey round us.
How long, Lord? You go dey angry forever? Your jealousy go burn like fire?
Pour out your wrath on di nations wey no know you, and on di kingdoms wey no call on your name,
because dem don devour Jacob and lay waste im dwelling place.
No hold di iniquities of our papa dem against us. Make your tender mercies quickly meet us, because we dey brought very low.
Help us, God of our salvation, for di glory of your name. Deliver us and forgive our sins for your name sake.
Why di nations go talk say, “Where dem God dey?” Make di vengeance for di blood of your servants wey dem don pour out dey known among di nations for our sight.
Make di groaning of di prisoner come before you. According to di greatness of your power, preserve dem wey dem don appoint to die.
Pay back to our neighbors seven times for dem bosom di reproach wey dem don reproach you, Lord.
So we, your people and di sheep of your pasture, go give you thanks forever. We go tell your praise to all generations.

chapters.title: For di Chief Musician. To di tune of Lilies of di Covenant. By Asaph. A Psalm.

verses.text: Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you wey lead Joseph like flock, you wey sit above di cherubim, shine out.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might and come to save us.
Restore us again, God. Make your face shine, and we go dey saved.
Lord God of Armies, how long you go dey angry against di prayer of your people?
You don feed dem with di bread of tears and give dem tears to drink for large measure.
You make us cause of strife for our neighbors, and our enemies dey laugh among dem self.
Restore us again, God of Armies. Make your face shine, and we go dey saved.
You bring vine out of Egypt. You drive out di nations and plant am.
You clear di ground for am. E take root and fill di land.
Di mountains cover with im shadow, and im branches be like di mighty cedars.
E send out im branches to di sea and im shoots to di River.
Why you don break down im walls, so dat all wey pass dey pick im fruit?
Di boar from di forest dey ruin am. Di wild animals of di field dey feed on am.
Return, we beg you, God of Armies. Look down from heaven and see, and visit dis vine,
di stock wey your right hand don plant, and di son wey you don make strong for yourself.
Dem don burn am with fire. Dem don cut am down. Dem perish at di rebuke of your face.
Make your hand dey on di man of your right hand, on di son of man wey you don make strong for yourself.
So we no go turn back from you. Revive us, and we go call on your name.
Restore us again, Lord God of Armies. Make your face shine, and we go dey saved.
